audit.why: 45.33% over 514 games with HARD 7.5/10 and Irelia carry threat 9/10 — the difficulty framing is right even though the chart under it was not.
audit.corrected: No difficulty change; the chart was the problem, not the rating.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four chart rows disagreed with the audited mirror: level 1 was given to Irelia while the page's own why said Quinn out-trades her there, and the item stages were given to Quinn on a 45% lane.
audit.why: Irelia has no Bladesurge reset target at levels 1-2, so those are Quinn's; level 3 and the first-item window are even once Flawless Duet and Defiant Dance exist.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 2 and 5 flipped as one atomic group in both layers to Quinn / Quinn / Skill / Skill, ratings set to 7/10 on the Quinn rows and 5/10 on the even ones (inverse of the mirror's 3/10 and 5/10), and each phases[N].why rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry repeatedly says the blind blanks her 'auto-shred' and tells you to 'E-knockback over her'; nothing says Flawless Duet ends Behind Enemy Lines.
audit.why: Blinding Assault (Q, 11s at rank 1) marks and hinders vision — it is not an attack blind and it is not Vault. Vault (E, 12s) is a dash that briefly interrupts her and lands Quinn at her own attack range; there is no knockback and no leaping over her. Flawless Duet stuns, and Behind Enemy Lines is a flagged channel, so her 16s E cancels the ultimate outright. Bladesurge refreshes on a Marked target, which is why her E-then-Q chain is the real threat.
audit.corrected: Named the real cooldowns, put the channel cancel on the interactions line, and replaced every knockback and blind claim.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys and all three prose stages are in the first person.
audit.why: The site's coaching voice is second person.
audit.corrected: Rewritten in second person at the same length.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are the only stretch I truly own here. My range plus Harrier auto-resets let me chunk her before her Q has reset targets, and my Q blind can blank her auto-shred passive if I time it on her stepping up. The trick: don't blow Q early — bait her first Q dash, then E-knockback over her and blind her follow-up. If I trade clean and deny her early Q resets, she has nothing yet.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are the only stretch you truly own. Your range plus Harrier auto-resets chunk her before Bladesurge has reset targets, and Blinding Assault hinders her vision on the step-up. The trick: don't blow it early — bait the first Bladesurge, then Vault, which interrupts her and drops you a full attack range clear. Deny those early resets and she has nothing yet.

edits.before: By 4-5 I still keep a plate-and-poke edge, but level 6 is where this flips. My R is roam, not burst, so it does nothing for the actual duel, while she hits a real item and her Q-dash-reset-into-E-stun chain comes online. Once she can W-block my Harrier burst and stun me mid-kite, I can't trade straight up. Use 6 to roam or shove and crash, not to fight her even.
edits.after: By 4-5 you keep a plate-and-poke edge, but 6 is where this flips. Your R is roam, not burst, so it does nothing for the duel, while she hits a real item and the Flawless Duet into Bladesurge chain. Once Defiant Dance eats your Harrier burst and her 16s stun ends your ultimate, you cannot trade straight. Use 6 to roam or crash, not to fight her even.

edits.before: If I snowballed early, my lethality/crit and roam can still pick her off when she's isolated — that's my 2+ item window on paper. But be honest: if Irelia got going, she Q-resets through any fight, W-blocks my burst, and her passive shred melts my squishy frame. I have no front-to-back threat. The whole game plan is win lane, snowball the map with R, and end before she stat-checks me in every skirmish.
edits.after: If you snowballed early, your lethality/crit and roam still pick her off when she is isolated — that is the 2+ item window on paper. But be honest: a fed Irelia resets Bladesurge through any fight, blunts your burst with Defiant Dance, and her passive shred melts you. You have no front-to-back threat. Win lane, snowball the map with R, and end before she stat-checks every skirmish.
